title: PCP shared definitions
description: Types shared by every PCP frame: ids, timestamps, users, rooms, scopes, message content elements, media and sticker references, members. Objects allow unknown properties so that additive protocol changes never break older validators (see spec/PCP.md, Versioning).

Id.description: Opaque identifier. Frame ids, message ids, session ids, blob ids. ULIDs recommended for frame ids.

Timestamp.description: RFC 3339 date-time in UTC with millisecond precision recommended, e.g. 2026-10-05T18:04:11.532Z.

TypeName.description: Event or action type. Dotted lowercase segments. Vendor extensions use the x.<platform>. prefix.

Platform.description: Platform name: camfrog, discord, twitch, telegram, patv, ...

Seq.description: Per-session sequence number assigned by the connector to every event and result frame. Starts at 1, strictly increasing by 1.

Ext.description: Platform-specific extras, keyed by platform name. Modules that do not know a key ignore it. Never required for correct behaviour.

UserRef.description: A user on one platform. Global identity key is (scope.platform, id). The identity service maps that pair to a PATV account.

id.description: Stable external id. Camfrog: the login lowercased. Discord: snowflake. Twitch: numeric user id.

login.description: Account/login name as the platform spells it (Camfrog login, Discord username, Twitch login). Used for platform commands such as /kick.

display.description: Human-facing display name, markup stripped. May differ from login and may change at any time; never use it as a key.

display_raw.description: Display name exactly as the platform delivered it, including markup (Camfrog ..).

is_self.description: True when this is the connector's own bot account.

is_bot.description: True when the platform or connector knows this is an automated account (room bots).

resolved_by.description: (1.1) How the connector tied this user to the account: login (an in-packet login, or one confirmed in the same tick), display (matched by display name), memory (remembered from earlier), unresolved. Open: an unknown value means 'not login-resolved'. Only login-resolved users may act as an account at a hub (spec/PCP.md, Users).

unresolved.description: (1.1) The connector has only a display name. id is then a session-scoped opaque token (e.g. ~<display>#<session>), never a login: presence and rendering only; receivers never create or match identities on it.

anonymous.description: (1.1) A user reported only as anonymous presence (privacy edge filter). id is a short-lived opaque token (e.g. anon-<hex>): presence only, never an identity.

RoomRef.description: A room, channel, thread or DM conversation.

id.description: Stable external id. Camfrog: the room id from the JOIN packet (not the window title). Discord: channel snowflake. Twitch: broadcaster user id.

parent_id.description: Parent channel of a thread, or category of a channel.

RoomTarget.description: A room named by id and/or display name (used by room.join, where the caller may only know the display name).

GuildRef.description: A server/workspace that contains rooms (Discord guild). Absent on platforms without one.

Scope.description: Where something happens. platform is always present. room is absent only for connector-wide events (presence, inbox, status).

MediaRef.description: Reference to binary media. Bytes never travel inside a PCP frame except tiny inline data. 'blob' names an object in the runtime's blob store (uploaded by the connector before the frame is sent, see spec/PCP.md, Media); 'url' is any fetchable location.

data.description: Inline base64, at most 64 KiB decoded (87384 chars).

Element.description: One message content element (Satori-style). Unknown element types are allowed and must carry a plain-text fallback in 'text' when they have a textual rendering.

allOf.$comment: (1.1) elements below. Each carries a plain-text rendering in 'text', so 1.0 receivers and connectors that do not render them natively show that instead.

fmt.description: Display style hint (Discord-style letters: t T d D f F R). Open.

slug.description: A room on a bridge hub, by its public slug.

ref.description: Opaque reference of an anonymous gift or tip.

allOf.$comment: (1.1) An anonymous giver has only an opaque ref: no from and no tx. A named giver has from and tx and no ref.

ref.description: Card id at the hub; card.update names it.

v.description: Card version; card.update carries a higher one.

cl.description: Card layout language version (1 = the first one). A renderer that does not know it shows text.

layout.description: Declarative layout, at most 6 KB serialised. Opaque to PCP.

state.description: Current state the layout binds to, at most 2 KB serialised. Opaque to PCP.

text.description: Text path for platforms without components, e.g. the command to type.

key.description: Dotted key of a hub system line (e.g. topic.set); receivers that do not know it show text.

MemberGroup.description: Where a member sits in the room's list. Camfrog: members (on cam) / lurkers (off cam) / viewing. Platforms without groups omit it.

Text.description: Plain text. Connectors split over-long outbound text according to limits.message_max_chars.

Points.description: (1.1) A whole number of a hub's points (tips, prices), as a decimal string so no JSON number precision is lost. Points, not money.

Emoji.description: A reaction emoji: unicode name/character, plus the platform id of a custom one.

HmacId.description: (1.1) A pseudonymous identity reference: the first 20 lowercase hex characters of HMAC-SHA256(key, UTF-8 of platform + ":" + id), where id is the UserRef.id exactly as the connector reports it (no normalisation) and the key is the one named by the carrying frame's hidden_kid (spec/PCP.md, Privacy edge filter; the section has a test vector).

BindingMode.description: (1.1) How a bridge hub uses a remote room: ingest (remote -> hub only), relay (both ways), mirror (hub -> remote only), off, bot_only (no hub room; bots only).

NameSource.description: (1.1) Where a relayed author's name comes from: the hub display name, the author's linked login on the target platform, or the author's unique hub handle.

RelayAuthor.description: (1.1) The person a relay action speaks for. Connectors render {name} from name only, never from display.

acct.description: The author's account id at the hub (opaque).

handle.description: The author's unique hub handle (what a block or reply command takes).

tag.description: Short origin tag rendered beside the name (e.g. web, discord).

identities.description: At most one entry: the author's linked identity on the receiving connector's own platform (its external id there), so the connector can apply its own per-user checks (ignore lists, timeouts). Hubs MUST NOT send links to other platforms (spec/PCP.md, Relay).

BindingTarget.description: (1.1) Action routing on a bridge hub with several bindings: a binding id, or "native" for the hub's own room.

Phase.description: (1.1) Progress of a long-running action in interim results (queued, waiting, playing, live, ...). Open: unknown values mean 'still running'.

CmdInvocation.description: (1.1) The text path of an interactive input: the command a platform without components types instead.

Input.description: (1.1) One input of an actions element: button, select or amount (open; unknown kinds render as their cmd). custom_id is 1-64 printable ASCII characters, so at most 64 bytes (module:entity:verb:version). A select needs at least one option.

label_key.description: Catalog key of the label; label is the rendered text.

CustomId.description: (1.1) Id of an interactive input: 1-64 printable ASCII characters (module:entity:verb:version), so characters equal bytes and the id passes Telegram callback_data (64 bytes) unchanged.
